entries.name: Normally open —| |—
entries.description: Pass a path when the selected bit is TRUE.
entries.example:
Path 1: | | SW1
All paths join → ( LAMP )
entries.output: LAMP ON for the example switch states
entries.note: Toggle SW1 ON to close this program contact. It checks a bit, rather than describing a physical switch’s wiring.

entries.name: Normally closed —|/|—
entries.description: Pass a path when the selected bit is FALSE.
entries.example:
Path 1: |/| SW1
All paths join → ( LAMP )
entries.output: LAMP OFF for the example switch states

entries.name: Series paths = AND
entries.example:
Path 1: | | SW1 — | | SW2
All paths join → ( LAMP )
entries.output: LAMP OFF for the example switch states

entries.name: Parallel paths = OR
entries.example:
Path 1: | | SW1
Path 2: | | SW2
All paths join → ( LAMP )
entries.output: LAMP ON for the example switch states

entries.name: LAMP coil —( )—
entries.description: Use the combined path result for the output.
entries.example:
Path 1: | | SW1
All paths join → ( LAMP )
entries.output: LAMP ON for the example switch states
entries.note: Parallel paths join before one output coil. With no paths, this teaching lab keeps the output OFF.

entries.name: LAMP := SW1;
entries.description: Assign a Boolean expression to LAMP.
entries.output: LAMP ON for the example switch states
entries.note: := assigns a value. A semicolon finishes the instruction. SW1, SW2 and LAMP are predefined BOOLs here.
